gloss: to cause trouble; to make waves; to stir things up

definitions.gloss: to cause trouble; to make waves; to stir things up
definitions.explanation: To disturb a peaceful situation by creating conflict or controversy. Literally 'to raise waves and wind.' Often used in the negative to advise against creating unnecessary conflict.

examples.japanese: {波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to make waves.

examples.japanese: あまり{波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てないほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better not to stir things up too much.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{一言|ひとこと}が{職場|しょくば}に{波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てることになった。
examples.english: His single remark ended up causing trouble at the workplace.

notes:
USAGE:
Very commonly used in the negative form ({波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てない) to express the desire to avoid conflict. Reflects the Japanese cultural value of maintaining harmony ({和|わ}). The related expression {波風|なみかぜ}が{立|た}つ describes the intransitive version — trouble arising on its own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波風|なみかぜ}を{立|た}てない (to not make waves)
- {波風|なみかぜ}が{立|た}つ (waves arise; trouble brews)
- {波風|なみかぜ}の{立|た}たない{生活|せいかつ} (a peaceful life without trouble)
